hypotheses.title: Lambda capture entries make every stage-5 variable lookup O(#lambdas): binding lookup re-probes capture groups and recomputes per-lookup invariants at each entry
hypotheses.issue: Each explicit lambda in a function body pushes a non-empty capture entry (addCaptureGroup) onto the function's narrowing chain in resolveLambdaFunctionExpr, and it stays there for the rest of the function. Every later variable/function reference goes through lookupBinding -> lookupBindingInner, which recursively walks the whole chain. At EVERY capture entry it calls isStableDeclaration(t, ref) (a sync.Map load in unnarrowedSymbol plus ValueSymbolMetadata/GetSymbol under the env-wide symbolSpacesMu RWMutex), recomputes t.unnarrowedSymbol(ref), and probes CaptureGroupContains (another env-wide RWMutex in capturegroups.Store.Contains). This happens even when the ref has no narrowing entry at all, i.e. when the capture check cannot change the result. None of the checks except CaptureGroupContains depend on the entry. A function with N closures followed by N references does O(N^2) entry visits, each with several map/lock operations. In a CPU profile at N=4000, lookupBindingInner is ~60% of the CPU and isStableDeclaration ~30%. sync/atomic Int32.Add from RWMutex reader counts is 19% flat. Local Type Resolution grows ~3.5x per doubling of N and is ~80% of compile time at N=4000.

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate closures<N>.bal: N lambdas capturing a mutable local, then N calls.
Each lambda pushes a capture entry onto the narrowing chain; every later
variable reference walks all of them (lookupBindingInner), => O(N^2)."""
import sys
n = int(sys.argv[1])
out = ['import ballerina/io;', '', 'public function main() {', '    int x = 0;']
for i in range(n):
    out.append(f'    function () returns int c{i} = function () returns int {{ return x % 1000 + {i}; }};')
for i in range(n):
    out.append(f'    x += c{i}();')
out += ['    io:println(x);', '}']
open(f'closures{n}.bal', 'w').write('\n'.join(out) + '\n')
reproducer.command: python3 gen_closures.py 4000 && go build -o bal ./cli/cmd && ./bal run --stats closures4000.bal   # see Analysis / Local Type Resolution

hypotheses.fix_approach: Split lookupBindingInner in two. First, an iterative findBinding walks the chain with only pointer and flag comparisons, skipping capture entries, to find the nearest entry for ref (it keeps the function-boundary/query-aggregated rule). Then unnarrowedSymbol and isStableDeclaration are computed ONCE per lookup. If the result is already the unnarrowed base and not narrowed (the common case: ref was never narrowed), or the ref is stable, the capture probes are skipped entirely, because they can only return (base, false). Otherwise only the capture entries between the chain head and the matched entry are probed. Behaviour is preserved: the original returned (unnarrowedSymbol(ref), false) at the first containing capture, which equals the no-capture result whenever effective==base and !isNarrowed. Pitfall: when ref is itself a narrowed symbol with no entry, effective==ref!=base, so the probe is still needed. The prototype still walks the chain once per lookup (O(N) cheap pointer hops), so it remains technically quadratic with a much smaller constant. A complete fix could also track per function which bases have any narrowing entry, to skip the walk entirely, and make capture-group membership lock-free (groups are immutable once built). canNarrow's capture walk was left untouched. make test passed.
